findings.reason: the predicate's contract must join the document unit alongside the sections (or §8's authored-change coverage is silently dropped in the rewrite of `_plan_review_pending`), which changes both the predicate and its done-when.
findings.text: the coverage predicate §16 describes asks the whole-document question first and, when no stored record matches whole, joins only the outstanding implementable sections (§18's reader) to the union of stored section digests; it never consults the document unit that `_section_digests` also produces, so an edit to a decision, a followup or an authored comment moves the whole-document digest but leaves every section covered and composes no review — directly contradicting §16's own claim that such an edit "earns a review exactly as §8 requires"

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — the coverage predicate §16 introduces hides substantial behaviour ("any authored change earns a review", per §8) behind an interface that cannot express it: it joins only the outstanding implementable sections, never the document unit the same digest map also carries.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the plan's shape is consolidation and it names each owner to extend (the tag expression and the span parser in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, the identity derivation in `reckon/crew/routing.py`, the store's card recogniser) and retires the store's copies instead of forking them; the two projections of the one private read are justified by spans no heading record describes.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1478, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 names its one added public definition (`strip_tags`) and that nothing is retired, §17 names its two (`plan_headings` and the machinery-element predicate) and states `landed_section_ids` is a move and no public definition can retire, and neither section adds to cli_options, mcp_views or refusal_families (§16 reuses the existing plan-review-missing refusal family). Note (not a finding): §16's prose says the three sections "grow the family by four", but §18's addition is already inside the cited 1478, so the implementable §16+§17 delta is three, which the per-section done-whens state correctly.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names machinery the code confirms and extends it rather than rebuilding: `_plan_html._TAG_RE` and `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` (reckon/_plan_html.py:1506, :44), `_store._landed_card_span`/`_is_structural_boundary`/`landed_section_ids` and the heading helpers (reckon/_store.py:1033, :875, :1075, :901, :940, :973), `plan_review._PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`/`_AuthoredProseParser` (reckon/crew/plan_review.py:147, :168), the AST rule machinery in `interface_counts.read_trees`/`_staged_writes` (reckon/interface_counts.py:441, :97), and `routing.section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates` (reckon/crew/routing.py:224, :243). Each proposed change is an extension of an existing owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — every layer the plan adds states the machinery it extends and why the extension is the honest change (`strip_tags` over the existing `_TAG_RE`; the machinery-element predicate over the `data-reckon` attribute read in five files; `plan_headings` as the public projection of the private span parser), rather than a parallel implementation.
